content: Between every two pines there is a door to a new world.
author: John Muir
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, John Muir saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: What lesson in endurance or renewal can you draw from the natural world today?
